statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rhabdo-Seq, by detecting PAX3 or PAX7 translocations with FOXO1, identified ctDNA in 27 of the 49 FP-RMS cases.
statements.evidence: Identification of pathognomonic translocations between PAX3 or PAX7 and FOXO1 by Rhabdo-Seq was the best method for measuring ctDNA in FP-RMS and detected ctDNA in 27 of 49 cases (55%).
statements.note: Rhabdo-Seq detection of PAX3/PAX7-FOXO1 translocations found ctDNA in 27 of 49 FP-RMS cases (55%).

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Patients with FN-RMS whose ctDNA was detectable at diagnosis had lower event-free and overall survival than FN-RMS patients without detectable ctDNA.
statements.evidence: Patients with FN-RMS with detectable ctDNA at diagnosis had significantly worse outcomes than patients without detectable ctDNA (event-free survival, 33.3% v 68.9%; P = .0028; overall survival, 33.3% v 83.2%; P < .0001)
statements.note: In FN-RMS, event-free survival was 33.3% versus 68.9% and overall survival 33.3% versus 83.2% with versus without detectable ctDNA.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose ctDNA became undetectable during therapy had longer event-free survival than those with persistent ctDNA.
statements.evidence: Pretreatment serum and tumor samples were available from 124 patients with newly diagnosed IR RMS from the Children's Oncology Group biorepository
statements.note: Only pretreatment samples were analysed, so the abstract says nothing about how ctDNA changes during therapy relate to survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After multivariable adjustment, ctDNA stayed independently linked to poor prognosis in FN-RMS, but not in the FP-RMS cohort.
statements.evidence: In multivariable analysis, ctDNA was independently associated with worse prognosis in FN-RMS but not in the smaller FP-RMS cohort.
statements.note: In multivariable analysis ctDNA was an independent prognostic factor in FN-RMS but not in the smaller FP-RMS cohort.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Basal cfDNA carried 300 of the 411 alterations identified in diagnostic tissue, a 73% overlap.

statements.note: The abstract reports that 73% (300/411) of tissue alterations were also identified in basal cfDNA.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Patients who progressed within 24 months of diagnosis had higher pretreatment ctDNA levels, in haploid genome equivalents per milliliter of plasma, than patients without such progression.
statements.evidence: Pretreatment ctDNA levels, as haploid genome equivalents per milliliter of plasma, were higher in patients without CR (P = 0.02) and in POD24-pos patients compared with POD24-neg patients (P < 0.001).
statements.note: Pretreatment ctDNA levels were higher in POD24-pos than in POD24-neg patients (P < 0.001).

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Treatment brought a steep fall in ctDNA levels, especially pronounced among patients with complete response and among POD24-neg patients.
statements.evidence: Dynamic analysis showed that ctDNA levels decreased dramatically after treatment, although the reduction was more significant in patients with CR and POD24-neg patients.
statements.note: ctDNA levels decreased dramatically after treatment, with a more significant reduction in patients with CR and in POD24-neg patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Occult cancer was found in 52 of the 107 participants in the initial cohort, nearly half of them.
statements.evidence: Cancer was present in 52 of the 107 participants in the initial cohort (48.6%).
statements.note: Cancer was present in 52 of the 107 participants (48.6%) in the initial cohort.

statements.label: supported

statements.note: 47 of the 49 participants with combined gains and losses across three or more chromosomes had cancer (95.9%).

statements.label: supported

statements.note: Whole-body MRI had a sensitivity of 98.0% and a specificity of 88.5%, so sensitivity was the higher of the two.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In real-world data, anticoagulation in patients with detectable ctDNA was associated with an adjusted hazard ratio for VTE of 0.50.

statements.note: Among 2,522 real-world patients with detected ctDNA, anticoagulation was associated with lower VTE rates (adjusted HR 0.50).

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across the discovery, validation and generalizability cohorts, the liquid-biopsy machine learning model achieved higher c-indices than the Khorana score.
statements.evidence: A machine learning model trained on liquid biopsy data outperformed previous risk scores (discovery, validation and generalizability c-indices 0.74, 0.73 and 0.67, respectively, versus 0.57, 0.61 and 0.54 for the Khorana score)
statements.note: The liquid-biopsy model's c-indices (0.74, 0.73, 0.67) exceeded those of the Khorana score (0.57, 0.61, 0.54) in all three cohorts.
